examples.before:
date: 2024-01-15
big: 1_000
flag: yes
switch: on
octal: 0o17
legacy: 017
hex: 0x1F
sexa: 1:30
exp: 1e3
inf: .inf
nul: ~
num: +12
examples.input: `config history` (the starting file is imported and each value's type is shown)

results.1: exit 0. All six arms agree on everything except `inf`: date -> "2024-01-15" (text), big -> "1_000" (text), flag -> "yes" (text), switch -> "on" (text), octal -> 15, legacy -> 17 (decimal, not octal), hex -> 31, sexa -> "1:30" (text), exp -> 1000.0, nul -> null, num -> 12. For `inf`, two arms give ".inf" (text) and four arms give `Infinity`, a bare token in the history output.
All six arms: exit 0. The file gains the line `when: 2024-02-01`, and history records "2024-02-01" as text, not a date.

All six arms: exit 0, and history records old "yes" -> new 31. Three arms rewrite your input, so the file now reads:
flag: 31
The other three keep your spelling, so the file now reads:
flag: 0x1F

One arm: exit 0. The file gains `retry: -1e3`, and history records -1000.0. Five arms: exit 2 and nothing is stored, because `-1e3` is taken as an option and the error says the value argument is missing. The message wording differs between arms, and two of them also print the usage text.

context.in_practice: Each of the six arms behaved differently somewhere. Plain words such as dates, `yes`/`on`, `1_000` and `1:30` reliably stay text, and hex, `0o` octal and `1e3` become numbers. However, `.inf` is text in some arms and `Infinity` in others. Setting a hex number rewrites the file to `31` in half the arms. Only one arm accepts a negative number like `-1e3` as a value; in the rest it fails as a missing argument.
context.stakes: This choice decides what a hand-written value in troupe.yml becomes when the tool reads it. For example, it decides whether `2024-01-15` stays text or becomes a date, whether `yes` or `on` becomes a boolean, and whether `.inf` becomes a number. It also decides whether `config set` stores what you typed or rewrites it.
context.tradeoff: Route 1: one set of typing rules for both the file and typed values. The cost is that edge cases (`.inf`, whether hex input is kept as typed, values with a leading `-`) came out differently from arm to arm.

plan_why: Shows how plain scalars are typed under the YAML 1.2 core schema, both in the file and in VALUE: dates, 1_000, yes, 017, 0o17, 0x1F, 1:30, 1e3, .inf and ~. The JSON 'old'/'new' values in history show whether each became a string, int, float, bool or null, and the set commands show how new values are typed and quoted when written back.
routes: Own YAML 1.2 core-schema resolver for both file values and VALUE
